$comment: Every architecture rule Broiler.VM names, with how much it currently proves.
Milestone VM-1's exit gate asks that the contract be implemented and proven against the
fixture profile. A rule can be expressed long before the checkout contains anything able to
violate it, and a register that did not say so would let a passing suite read as stronger
evidence than it is. Roadmap section 16 makes an untruthful support claim a stop condition and
the status ledger's update rule 4 forbids promoting a shell result, so every rule carries its
status and the evidence bundle repeats the counts.
ONE CRITERION, APPLIED TO EVERY ROW. `status` describes the GRAPH: can anything in the current
checkout violate this rule? `witness` records a real violating input, and every rule has one
regardless of status - a Vacuous rule is one nothing in the component can break, not one that
was never shown working.
Status values, and nothing else: Active, Vacuous, Deferred.
Active   - something in the checkout could violate it, and a witness shows it rejecting one.
Vacuous  - it runs and is witnessed, but nothing in the graph can violate it. Not a defect:
the honest state of a rule whose subject cannot yet be broken.
Deferred - not asserted; the activation milestone owns promoting it.
A Deferred or Vacuous row may never name an activation milestone at or before the current
milestone, and a rule whose activation milestone IS the current milestone must be Active with a
passing witness. RuleRegisterTests enforces the register against the test methods and the
witness inputs in both directions.
WHAT VM-1 CHANGED. Five of the six rows that named VM-1 as their activation milestone are
promoted: the product graph now has method bodies, assembly references and an exported surface,
so B2, B4, B5b, B6 and B7 each have something that could break them. B3 is the one row where
the honest answer is different, and it is recorded rather than papered over - see its own row.
Rule E5 is superseded: it fused a cardinality claim about the graph with a member claim about
one type, and only the first is falsified by VM-1. V1 replaces the first; V2 preserves the
second verbatim.

REVIEW PASS. An adversarial review after the first implementation returned 45 findings that survived refutation, 16 of them blockers. Two register rows were among them: V4 checked a property count rather than the frozen rows it claimed to check, and V9 asserted static return types rather than the construction site. Both statements and both rules were corrected here. A rule weaker than its own statement is the defect this register exists to prevent, so those two are recorded rather than quietly tightened.

GROUP H, THE HUMAN-REVIEW RECORD RULES. The review documents - HUMAN_REVIEW.md, the evidence-bundle READMEs and the status ledger - carry marks, identifiers and figures, and every one of them is a claim about something else in the checkout. Unbound they rot, and this component has already found a transposed byte figure, two stale test counts and a worksheet citation pointing at a line the annotations had turned into a parameter declaration. H1 closes the mark vocabulary against the legend, H2 holds every cited exclusion to a definition in a bundle's exclusion table, H3 refuses a source line number anywhere in a review document and holds the generated record's coverage table to the tree it describes, H4 refuses a record stating a decision the annotations do not hold, and H5 binds every quoted headline figure to the log the bundle retains for it. H3 AND H4 WERE RESTATED WHEN THE RECORD BECAME A GENERATED ARTEFACT. A reviewer now writes in one place - the Broiler-Human line on the declaration they read - and HUMAN_REVIEW.md is computed from those lines, so the per-item worksheet those two rules were written against is deleted along with its rotting citations, and the attestation they guarded no longer exists. The risks are unchanged and are answered against the new mechanism: a review route that has quietly lost an area is a coverage table that has quietly lost a file, and a ticked APPROVED box over unfilled fields is a status word the states do not give.

Group H replaces a group R that was written and reverted, for two reasons that are recorded rather than forgotten. First, R1..R6 is a reserved namespace: ADR 0003 records that R1..R6 are ADR 0012's six ownership roles, and renames another set away from R1..R5 for exactly that reason. H is unused across every record and the roadmap. Second, every rule in that attempt was weaker than its own statement, and an adversarial pass broke all five by editing the tree and watching the suite stay green - a capped token regex, a definition scanner that accepted any table row, an area set derived from the document under test, an attestation field list read off whatever bullets were present, and an image-size check that passed when the two sizes were exchanged. Each of those is named in the rule's own remarks and carries its own witness. Group H witnesses are per CLAUSE, not per rule: the single worst defect of the reverted attempt was asserting every witness with a bare non-empty check over an input that violated several clauses at once, which pinned only whichever clause fired first and let four independent clauses be deleted in one patch.

All five name owningAdr 0012, which owns the support-claim and ownership surface they protect. That is a NOMINAL owner and the only such row in this register: ADR 0012 is frozen and names none of them, while every other row names a record that states its rule. Exclusion EX-53 records it rather than letting the field imply a binding that does not exist.

A SECOND ADVERSARIAL PASS, AGAINST GROUP H ITSELF. Three reviewers attacked the five rules by constructing violating inputs, running the suite and recording what stayed green; every escape they found is closed here or recorded as a limit. Four shapes recurred and are worth naming, because they are shapes and not one-off slips. A section lookup that returned its first match and never asked whether it was the only one made every rule readable from a decoy heading, which is how an APPROVED record over four unsigned attestation fields passed; sections are now required to be unique. A markdown reader that gated on the leading pipe, or on the absence of a block quote, put whole rows and whole list items outside every rule that read them. A definition scanner told to read a section rather than a TABLE accepted anything appended to the end of a bundle, code fences included. And a clause with no witness of its own is a clause that can be deleted in the same patch as three others with nothing red - which is why every phrasing, every enumeration member and every placeholder word now has an input that names it. The register's own witness column was among the findings: exchanging two rows' witness fields wholesale satisfied every check that read them, so a witness named for a rule is now held to the row it sits in, and the orphan check compares whole paths rather than asking whether some row's witness string contained the file name.

GROUP J, THE CODE-ASSURANCE RULES. Every relevant product unit carries the policy's two-line review block; every generated header, CODE-ASSURANCE.md, HUMAN_REVIEW.md and assurance.manifest.json is written from the tree; and NOTHING in this component has been reviewed by a human. Group J is what keeps that record honest in both directions. J1 holds coverage to the exemption predicate, J2 holds every field to its closed vocabulary and reports a block that parses as nothing, J3 binds each recorded fingerprint to the declaration it describes, J4 refuses any approval a human did not make, J5 holds every generated artefact to what the generator would write, J6 forbids a preprocessor directive in a covered file, J7 holds the manifest to the tree - every unit and every covered file whole - J8 holds every generated artefact to a declared shape so the generator cannot invent a sentence, J9 forbids review vocabulary the annotations do not support, J10 requires a falsification criterion where the assessment is highest, and J11 refuses a publish while the record says anything is unresolved. The letter J was chosen because A-E, V, F, M, G, P, S and T are in use, H is group R's replacement, and R1..R6 is the reserved namespace ADR 0003 records for ADR 0012's six ownership roles.

J4 IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. The value of this system at VM-1 is that it records the ABSENCE of review precisely; a mechanism that could turn PENDING into a name would convert an honest record of no review into a false one, and a false record is worse than none because it is trusted. The policy states that prohibition as a sentence about CI. Here it is an exception the generator throws, four separately witnessed transitions, and an assertion over the rendered text of every artefact rather than over the model that produced it - taking the artefact list as an argument, so that the assertion can be shown REJECTING one and cannot be emptied with the suite green.

J7 IS THE STRUCTURAL ONE, AND IT IS WHY THIS GROUP STOPPED BEING PATCHED. Three adversarial rounds produced 33 defeats and nearly every blocker lived in one place: the exemption predicate. A unit the predicate treats as trivial carries no annotation, therefore no fingerprint, therefore no record of any kind, so a semantic change to it was invisible to the whole system - and narrowing the predicate case by case failed three times, because each fix moved the same defeat one case over. The repair separates two questions that were fused. Whether a unit needs a human ANNOTATION is decided by the predicate, and that is unchanged. Whether a unit is WATCHED for change is not a question any more: every unit is, and assurance.manifest.json is the record. The manifest is a change-detection record and not a review; it is said in those words in the manifest's own header, in CODE-ASSURANCE.md and in J7's statement, so that a covered fingerprint is not read as a reviewed unit. The unit set was widened to match: every field declaration is a unit now, not only the const and static readonly ones, because a plain instance field's type is the width of the arithmetic the annotated bodies perform on it.

Group J witnesses are per CLAUSE, like group H's and for the same reason: a witness asserted with a bare non-empty check pins only whichever clause fires first, and four independent clauses can then be deleted in one patch with nothing red. Every assertion here names the CONTENT of the violation it expects. The witness inputs sit under witnesses/assurance/, and several of them carry the reviewer identifier WITNESS-ONLY, which is not a person and appears nowhere else - a rule about false approvals cannot be witnessed without an input that contains one. Each group J row is held to a FIXED EXPECTED TEXT rather than to a handful of required substrings, in all three of its prose fields. A substring check let a row CLAIM a capability the tests do not implement: a sentence saying CI compares every human line against the parent commit was appended to a row and stayed green, and no such mechanism exists anywhere in this component.

A FOURTH ROUND ATTACKED WHAT WAS LEFT, IN TWO GROUPS, AND BOTH ANSWERS ARE STRUCTURAL. The first group attacked the unit ENUMERATION rather than the exemption predicate. A unit exists only for a declaration kind the scanner names, so an enum member - which is how the budget dimensions and the reason codes are spelled - a type declaration header carrying a primary constructor, an event field declaration and an [assembly: InternalsVisibleTo] were each in no unit, no fingerprint and no manifest entry, with the suite green and assurance.manifest.json byte-unchanged. Widening the list answers three of the four and not the fourth, because an assembly-level attribute is a member of nothing and can never be a unit. So assurance.manifest.json gained a files array: one fingerprint per covered file, over the complete token stream of its compilation unit, held to the tree by J7 beside the units. Nothing in a covered file can change without something moving there, whatever kind of declaration it is. Comments are outside that stream because a token text is its own characters, which is what lets one generation stay a fixed point, and J7 asserts it rather than assuming it. The second group attacked the GENERATED ARTEFACTS. Two lines appended to AssuranceManifest.Header made the manifest assert reviewState=VERIFIED, humanReviewed=true, a named reviewer for all its entries and that the component was eligible for release - with both modes green and every source human line still reading PENDING - because J5 compares the file on disk against what the GENERATOR would write, and the generator would write exactly that. J8 and J9 are the answer. J8 holds every generated artefact line for line to a hand-maintained shape and re-derives every value by a different expression, which is also what finally pins AssuranceSummary.Worst behind the IP and Security rows of every file header. J9 forbids the review vocabulary outright unless the annotations support the occurrence, by the count they give for it or by a negation standing before it. The two are deliberately independent: J8 can be defeated by editing the shape as well as the generator, and J9 cannot be defeated by editing anything but its term list. The same pass replaced the forged-block recogniser, which was a literal-string whitelist that a differently worded block walked straight past.

Limits are recorded as exclusions rather than left implied: EX-60, narrowed: two lanes now run both modes, so what is left is that a lane fires on a pull request and on a tag and nothing compares a human line against its parent commit or binds an alias to a hosting identity; EX-61, that a six-hex fingerprint answers only whether a unit changed and is neither collision-free across units nor a cryptographic commitment; EX-62, that the exemption predicate decides relevance, so a unit it wrongly exempts is not reported by J1; EX-67, that the manifest detects a change and reviews nothing; EX-68, that the per-unit escape hatch is refused where it matters most and counted everywhere else, and judged nowhere; EX-69, that a file fingerprint says a file changed and not what changed in it; EX-70, that the declared shape of every generated artefact is a hand-maintained second copy, so a change made in both places passes; and EX-71, that J9 recognises a finite list of review terms and a claim worded outside it is not seen.

All eleven rows name owningAdr 0012, and that is NOMINAL, exactly as group H's is. ADR 0012 owns who is allowed to say yes and what may be said in public, which is this system's subject; it is frozen and names none of these rules. EX-53 is extended to cover both groups rather than duplicated.

rules.statement: No ProjectReference, resolved to a full path, lies outside the component root.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Any project file exists; the outbound half of the legacy boundary.

rules.statement: No PackageReference names a Broiler.* package.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Any project file exists; closes the feed-shaped reintroduction A1 cannot see.

rules.statement: No Compile, None, Content, EmbeddedResource or Import item resolves outside the component root.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Non-vacuous when any project declares one of the five item types; at VM-0 none does, so the sweep is empty and both witnesses carry the rule.

rules.statement: No product project has a ProjectReference resolving under src/tests/.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Broiler.VM.Fixtures exists at VM-0, so the forbidden target is present.

rules.statement: Every project under src/tests/ contains the literal element IsPackable false.
rules.evidence: Project file text, not the evaluated property
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Broiler.VM.Fixtures matches no name-suffix rule in the vendored packaging props and would otherwise default to packable.

rules.statement: Exactly three projects declare a PackageId, and for each PackageId equals AssemblyName equals RootNamespace equals the project file base name.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Three packable projects exist at VM-0.

rules.statement: The resolved ProjectReference edge multiset equals graph.manifest.json exactly; extra and missing edges both fail. Subsumes acyclicity.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Eight edges exist at VM-0.

rules.statement: No profile project references Broiler.VM.Runtime.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Broiler.VM.Fixtures is profile-shaped and exists at VM-0.

rules.statement: Broiler.VM.Runtime declares OutputType Library or omits it, and declares no composition root.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Broiler.VM.Runtime exists at VM-0.

rules.statement: No product project declares InternalsVisibleTo. VM-3 must prove a profile is writable through the public source contract alone.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Three product projects exist at VM-0.

rules.statement: No project outside the composition-root allow-list references an assembly matching Broiler.VM.Profile.*. The allow-list is empty at VM-0.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The allow-list is empty at VM-0, so any profile reference violates it.

rules.statement: Broiler.VM.Abstractions and Broiler.VM.Binary reference nothing outside the framework. The mechanical form of roadmap section 5's arrow to nothing.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Both assemblies are built at VM-0; the test assembly is the witness input.

rules.statement: Broiler.VM.Runtime references nothing outside Broiler.VM.Abstractions and Broiler.VM.Binary.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Broiler.VM.Runtime now uses types from both Abstractions and Binary - its meter implements Broiler.VM.IVmBoundedAllocationMeter and its verification path drives VmBoundedReader - so its AssemblyRef table names both and the rule is equality rather than subset.

rules.statement: No assembly in the product graph names a Broiler.* assembly outside the component's own set. The assembly-level twin of A1 and A2.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: A product assembly could name a foreign Broiler.* assembly. The subject now exists - the product graph names non-framework assemblies for the first time - but a VIOLATION is still unreachable: A1 forbids the outbound ProjectReference, A2 forbids the Broiler.* PackageReference, and the single-source NuGet.config makes such a package unresolvable, so no project in the checkout can acquire one. It becomes reachable at VM-3, when composition roots and profile packages exist. Exclusion EX-40 records the reasoning and the alternative that was rejected.
rules.witness: none - a witness needs a foreign Broiler assembly, and the graph is closed over its own seven. The project-file twins A1 and A2 are witnessed.

rules.statement: No exported member of a product assembly names a type outside System.* and Broiler.VM.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The product graph exports a contract surface whose members carry parameter and return types, so a foreign type on the public surface is now expressible.

rules.statement: No assembly in the product graph references a dynamic-loading, reflection-invocation or IL-emit API. Invariant 2 requires registration to be static and typed.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The witness is compiled into the test assembly, which the same scanner flags when pointed at it.

rules.statement: No assembly in the product graph applies ModuleInitializerAttribute. Invariant 2 forbids a module-initializer ordering dependency by name.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The product graph now declares method bodies, so a method could carry the attribute.

rules.statement: No product assembly references an assembly built from src/tests/.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: ApiBaselineWitnesses.FixtureReferenceWitness names a type from Broiler.VM.Fixtures - which is built from src/tests/ - so the test assembly emits the AssemblyRef the rule scans for. A project reference alone emits nothing: the compiler records only what is used, so without a real use the scanner would be pointed at an assembly that does not in fact hold the forbidden edge.

rules.statement: No product assembly exports a type named BuiltInProfiles, DefaultProfiles, AllProfiles or KnownProfiles. Roadmap section 3 rejects an aggregate profile type by name.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The product graph exports types other than VmCoreContract, so an aggregate profile type is now expressible.

rules.statement: dotnet pack over Broiler.VM.slnx produces exactly three .nupkg and three .snupkg, named for the three product assemblies.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: A component CI pack step exists. VM-0 creates no CI workflow; a manually executed pack log is retained in the evidence bundle as observed state, not as a rule assertion.

rules.statement: No produced .nuspec declares a dependency on a Broiler.* package outside the declared three.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: A component CI pack step exists.

rules.statement: No produced .nuspec's id, title, description, tags or release notes names a language. Implements roadmap section 14's packaging failure 'a language capability implied by package or API'.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: A component CI pack step exists.

rules.statement: No project file outside the component declares a ProjectReference or PackageReference resolving into Broiler.VM. The inbound half of the legacy boundary.
rules.evidence: Project files in an aggregate checkout above the component
rules.nonVacuousWhen: An aggregate checkout is present above the component root. Where none is, the rule reports INCONCLUSIVE rather than passing. Exclusion EX-01 records the conditionality.

rules.statement: VmCoreContract.Version and VmCoreContract.MinimumSupportedVersion equal the values in ADR 0003's header fields.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: ADR 0003 and VmCoreContract both exist at VM-0.

rules.statement: Every ADR file declares a Core contract header field, and the contract-bearing set is exactly 0002 through 0011.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Twelve ADR files exist at VM-0.

rules.statement: Every contract-bearing ADR declares the current core contract version.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Ten contract-bearing ADRs exist at VM-0.

rules.statement: The ADR index lists exactly the ADR files present, and every rule identifier named in an ADR has exactly one row in this register.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Twelve ADR files and this register exist at VM-0.

rules.statement: SUPERSEDED AT VM-1 by V1 and V2. As written it fused a cardinality claim about the graph (exactly one public type) with a member claim about one type (whose only members are the two contract-version constants). VM-1 necessarily falsifies the first and preserves the second. V1 replaces the cardinality half with an API baseline; V2 preserves the member half verbatim. The row is retained rather than removed so the supersession is auditable, and it asserts nothing.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Never again in this form; VM-6 owns removing the row when it freezes the public API.

rules.statement: The product graph exports every name the frozen public-name table fixes, and every exported type is declared in namespace Broiler.VM.
rules.evidence: Exported types against the frozen name baseline
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The product graph exports a contract surface. Replaces the cardinality half of E5. The witness points the rule at a graph exporting only the bounded-reading primitives which contains none of the frozen names.

rules.statement: VmCoreContract exports exactly Version and MinimumSupportedVersion, and both are literals.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: VmCoreContract exists. Preserves the member half of E5 verbatim.

rules.statement: No exported type or member uses a retired name, a struck bound name, or one of the six unqualified names the terminology rule bans.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The product graph exports a surface on which a retired name could appear.

rules.statement: VmProfileDescriptor declares exactly the thirty rows of the frozen table, by name, and none of the names excluded by construction.
rules.evidence: Compiled metadata against the frozen row list
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The descriptor exists as a type with properties. The rule compares row NAMES, not a count: a count is satisfied by any thirty-one properties at all, including thirty-one wrong ones, which is exactly the drift a table this long exists to catch.

rules.statement: Every reason in the registry maps to exactly one outcome category, derivably from its own value.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: VmReason and VmReasonRegistry exist. The witness is a reason value filed outside every category block which the derived mapping must reject.

rules.statement: The profile-facing metering surface declares exactly TryCharge, Poll, ReportRetained and ReportReleased, the charge amount is unsigned, and no member reads a remaining or effective value.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: IVmMeter exists.

rules.statement: No member on any exported type is named Grant, Refund, Reset, Extend, Increase, Raise, TopUp, Widen, Reopen, WithLimits, Withdraw or Credit.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The product graph exports members on which such a name could appear.

rules.statement: No public member returns Task, ValueTask or IAsyncEnumerable, and no product assembly calls a timer, delay or thread-abort API.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The product graph exports members with return types and declares method bodies.

rules.statement: Exactly one public member of the product graph mints a verified artifact, exactly one product assembly reaches that member, and the verification member takes exactly the descriptor, the byte span and a cancellation token.
rules.evidence: Compiled metadata: exported members, MemberRef tables, and the verification signature
rules.nonVacuousWhen: VmVerifiedArtifact and VmRuntime.Verify exist. Two halves, because either alone is weaker than the claim: counting members that return the handle would pass a graph with one factory and any number of assemblies calling it, and reading the member-reference tables says which assemblies can reach the factory at all. Neither half counts individual call sites, which would need an IL decoder; Exclusion EX-51 records that limit rather than letting the statement overreach.

rules.statement: No public member can express a persisted envelope, streaming or incremental verification, lazy per-section verification, or in-process producer input.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The product graph exports a surface on which such a member could appear.

rules.statement: Every mark token in a review document is one of the nine the legend publishes, and the legend publishes exactly those nine, once each. A mark token is a table cell whose whole trimmed text is bracketed, a bracketed token leading a list item, or the final token of an ATX heading - with or without backticks, and inside a block quote or not.
rules.evidence: HUMAN_REVIEW.md, any document under docs/review/, docs/evidence/*/README.md and docs/roadmap.status.md against a hard-coded set of nine
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The four review documents that exist - the generated HUMAN_REVIEW.md, the two evidence-bundle READMEs and the status ledger - carry marks in all three positions; docs/review/ is still enumerated and is now empty, the per-item worksheet that was its fifth member having been deleted with the review route it belonged to. The nine are hard-coded, never read from the document, and the legend is parsed independently of the body scan so that a tenth mark added to the legend is visible to the equality check. The token pattern carries NO length cap: capping it at six characters let [APPROVED], [REJECTED], [NOT MET] and [PENDING] through, which are the tokens an author actually reaches for. Rows are read with or without the optional leading pipe and with or without the optional trailing pipe, because GFM makes both optional and it is the delimiter row rather than either pipe that makes a table a table; gating the scan on the leading pipe let a whole row - a tenth legend mark among them - be skipped by dropping one character. Block-quote markers are stripped before a line is classified, so a quoted list item, table row or heading is still what it is; HUMAN_REVIEW.md opens with a quoted banner, so that is the document set's own idiom. Fenced code is not scanned, because an example is an illustration and not a claim. One carve-out, and only one: a GFM task-list checkbox - an unbackticked [ ], [x] or [X] leading a list item - is not a mark, because HUMAN_REVIEW.md section 1 rules that section 9's four-state decision list is written as ordinary markdown checkboxes and deliberately does not use this vocabulary. A bracketed token leading a list item in any other spelling is still a mark. No review document currently carries a mark in a heading, so both halves of that clause - backticked and bare - are carried by their witnesses alone. The legend is now a GENERATED section, which changes what this rule is worth rather than how it works: the nine marks are fixed text in AssuranceArtefactShape as well as in the generator, so publishing a tenth takes an edit in two places and still leaves this rule reading the corpus against the hard-coded nine.

rules.statement: Every EX- identifier cited in a review document is defined by a row of the section 9 exclusion table of an evidence bundle, or by a bolded list item in that section. A row of any OTHER table in section 9, a row in a subsection appended to section 9, and a row inside a fenced code block define nothing.
rules.evidence: The review documents against docs/evidence/*/README.md section 9
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Thirty-two exclusions are defined across the two bundles and cited from all five review documents. That figure had already drifted - it read twenty-six against a checkout carrying twenty-nine - and it is a count of a checkout rather than of a log, which is why nothing asserts it and why it is stated here rather than relied upon. Only the exclusion table defines, and only in section 9. A bundle also carries a gate table, an errata table, a negative-control table and a hash table, and accepting any table row whose first cell is an EX- identifier would let any of them launder an undefined citation; the table's own header is what decides, so a table that does not name an ID column and an Exclusion column defines nothing. Section 9 is the LAST section of a bundle and a section runs to the next heading at its own level or above, so being inside section 9 is not enough on its own: definitions stop at the first subheading, which is what keeps an errata or hash subsection appended to the end of the file out, and a fenced code block is not read at all, which is what stops a worked example minting the identifier it illustrates. The citation pattern accepts one digit as well as two, so EX-4 written for EX-04 - the commonest way this citation goes wrong - is reported rather than silently ignored, and it does not require a word boundary in front of the E, because an underscore is a word character and an anchored pattern could not see the italicised _EX-04_ at all. A citation inside a fenced code block is not read either, for the same reason a definition there is not: the two halves of the rule read the same document.

rules.statement: No review document cites a source file by line number, anywhere in its text. The generated review record's coverage table names every covered file exactly once, names nothing that is not a covered file, gives each file the number of relevant and unverified units the annotations give for it, and states the number of covered files the tree carries. The coverage section and the file-count row are each required to be unique.
rules.evidence: Every review document against a line-number citation scan, and HUMAN_REVIEW.md section 6 against AssuranceSources.Files and AssuranceScanner.Units
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Forty-five files are covered and the record carries forty-five rows, each asserted present by name, so a clean result is a comparison rather than a quantifier over nothing. The expectation is the covered file set and the annotations and is NOT DERIVED FROM THE DOCUMENT UNDER TEST - the property the eight-area enumeration had, and the reason it had it: an expectation read from the document under test agrees with it whatever it says, and deleting a whole risk area from both of its tables passed the rule this replaces. Six rejecting clauses are asserted by the content of the violation each expects - a covered file dropped, a file that is not covered named, a file named twice, a row whose figures the tree does not give, a second coverage heading, and a file count the tree does not carry - so they cannot be lost in one patch. Those six drive the real record with one thing altered, because a stored copy of a generated artefact would be a second copy of the thing under test, would go stale at every regeneration and would be repaired by regenerating it; the line-number clause has a witness file of its own, because a fragment that points at a line is generated by nothing. THIS RULE USED TO BE SOMETHING ELSE. It held a hand-written eight-area review route to a hand-written worksheet of numbered items, and the two to each other's counts. The worksheet is deleted: it cited source files by LINE NUMBER, its first item cited a checked multiplication that the annotations had turned into a parameter declaration, and this rule checked identifiers, areas and counts and never whether a citation meant anything. The line-number scan is the clause worth keeping and it was too narrow - it ran over that worksheet's Read rows alone, so a pointer in an evidence bundle or in the status ledger was read by nothing - and it now runs over every line of every review document. EX-55 closes with the worksheet: it recorded that nothing outside two documents said how many items the review ought to have, and the extent of the review is now the tree. THE FIRST LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: two of the eight columns are compared. The IP and Security columns are derived from assessments, and nothing anywhere holds an assessment to being true, which is EX-65 - rule J8 derives those two columns a second time from the same annotations, which is agreement and not truth. A SECOND LIMIT: the citation scan is a pattern over a backticked path followed by a number, so a pointer written without backticks, or as a URL fragment, is not seen.

rules.statement: The generated review record's status word is the aggregate the review states give, the two figures beside it are the annotations' figures, every alias the record names is one a Broiler-Human line in the product tree carries, no alias in the tree is left out of the record, and each alias's unit count is the number of human lines naming it. The status line and the alias section are each required to be unique.
rules.evidence: HUMAN_REVIEW.md's headline and section 5 against the states AssuranceStateMachine resolves and the aliases AssuranceHumanReview.AliasOn reads out of the human lines
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The clean direction over this checkout is a record that names nobody and states PENDING, which is the honest state and which the rule must not reject. That alone would be a rule nobody has watched work, so the accepting direction is asserted a second time over a synthesized tree that two people have read - rule J8's alias witness, shared exactly as A7 and A8 share one project file - in which the status is PARTIAL, one alias's decision answers to the code that is there and the other's has been outrun by it. Six rejecting clauses follow from that record, each asserted by the content of the violation it expects: a status word the states do not give, a figure the annotations do not give, a second status line, an invented alias, an alias dropped from the record, and a unit count the human lines do not support. THIS RULE USED TO BE SOMETHING ELSE AND ANSWERS THE SAME RISK. The record ended in a four-state decision list and a four-field attestation, and the cheapest false approval was to tick APPROVED over unfilled fields - or to delete the signature line, which the rule could not see until its field set was fixed to a closed enumeration. There is no attestation now: a decision is the Broiler-Human line on a declaration and the record is computed from those lines, so the same false record is reached by stating a status the states do not give, or by naming somebody no line names. WHAT A NAMED ALIAS STILL DOES NOT MEAN is that a person exists or that they read anything. An alias that reads plausibly and belongs to nobody is accepted here exactly as an invented name in the old attestation was: this rule holds the record to the tree, and nothing in this component holds the tree to a person. Rule J4 refuses an alias the TOOLING produced and cannot refuse one a human typed, and EX-60 records what would close it - a lane binding a reviewer declaration to a hosting identity and a pull request - and records it as absent. A SECOND LIMIT: the alias rows' Files, Current and Outrun columns are not compared here. The unit count is, and rule J8 derives all four a second time from the same human lines.

rules.statement: Every headline figure a review document quotes in a recognised phrasing matches the value in the log the evidence bundle retains for it: a suite total against the per-assembly Passed: totals in test.log or their sum, an architecture/behavioural split against the assembly each total names and in either word order, a Native AOT size against publish-aot.log, and a trimmed size against publish-jit-and-trimmed.log. The corpus must quote the current suite total, its split, its native image size and its trimmed image size at least once each, compared by value. A figure worded outside the recognised phrasings is not checked at all (EX-56). The rule checks document against LOG and not log against checkout: a stale log and a stale document agree with each other, and the bundle's expiry and recertification triggers are what cover that case (EX-54).
rules.evidence: The review documents against docs/evidence/vm-1/test.log, publish-aot.log and publish-jit-and-trimmed.log; a bundle README is compared against its own bundle's logs
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Three logs are retained and five documents quote figures from them. Each figure is bound to its own log and the split is bound per assembly, so exchanging the two image sizes - the likeliest form of this error, since the two numbers sit two lines apart in one sentence - fails twice rather than passing a set-membership check, and exchanging the two halves of the split fails whichever way round the halves are written. The four anti-deletion guards compare values; comparing patterns alone let the real figures be deleted while the VM-0 bundle's historical 35 passed kept the pattern alive, and the trimmed size had no guard at all, so nothing forced the corpus to keep quoting it once it had been reworded. TWO LIMITS, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED. First, the phrasing lists are finite and a figure worded outside them is not checked at all. They are kept minimal and non-overlapping and every entry is exercised by a witness sentence no other entry matches, so no entry can be deleted silently and no entry is decoration; what they do not cover is a genuine gap and not a hedge - a suite total qualified by an assembly word, as in the ledger's historical 35 architecture tests passed, is not recognised as a total. That is EX-56. Second, this rule cannot tell a stale log from a current one, which is EX-54.

rules.statement: Every relevant unit in the product graph carries a two-line Broiler Code Assurance annotation immediately above its declaration. A code unit is any member that can carry executable code, every field and event field declaration, every enum member, every delegate declaration and every type declaration. Relevance is decided by one declared exemption predicate, `AssuranceScanner.ExemptionFor`, over eight cases plus a per-unit escape hatch; a unit that predicate does not exempt and that carries no parsed block is named, whether the block was never written, written below the declaration instead of above it, or written as half a block. The per-unit `EXEMPT=<reason>` escape hatch may not be used in `Broiler.VM.Binary` at all, and every use of it anywhere is counted and named in `CODE-ASSURANCE.md`. The covered set is every `*.cs` file under a product project directory except the files in that project own `bin` and `obj` directories.
rules.evidence: The three product assemblies' source, as the generator would leave it, against `AssuranceScanner.ExemptionFor`, `AssuranceScanner.EscapeHatchViolations` and the annotation parser
rules.nonVacuousWhen: 689 relevant units and 903 exempt ones exist across 1,592 code units, so the exemption predicate answers both ways over the checkout and a clean result is a classification rather than a predicate that exempts everything. Every violating witness leaves the assurance comment IN the file, which is what makes the three worth witnessing separately: a coverage check that looked for the text rather than for the attachment would pass all of them. The accepting witnesses carry the other half - units the predicate covers, and one per-unit escape hatch - because a rule that named every unannotated unit regardless of the predicate would be a rule about comments rather than about review. THE LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: the exemption predicate decides relevance, so a unit it wrongly exempts is not reported by this rule. The rule cannot report a unit it was told not to look at. What answers that limit is no longer the predicate alone: rule J7 holds `assurance.manifest.json` to EVERY unit, exempt and relevant alike, and to every covered FILE whole, so a unit this rule cannot see is still watched for change even though nothing reviews it. That is EX-62, narrowed to what it now is. Five cases of the predicate were too broad and were narrowed, each with a witness of its own: case 2 asked only that the right-hand side of an assignment be SOME parameter of the constructor, so every permutation of a constructor body was exempt; case 3 accepted any argument that was a name or a constant, so a delegation supplying the LEB128 width or the budget dimension a charge lands in was exempt and the constant it supplied was the policy; case 1 accepted ANY member access, so `MaxSectionCount => _maxDeclaredCount` was trivial and the same permutation defeat survived one screen below the constructor fix, and case 3 readmitted exactly that shape until it required the same correspondence; case 5 whitelisted logical negation, so every `operator !=` in the component was a delegation to `Equals` when it is the opposite decision; and fields were not units at all, so a `const` budget could be multiplied by sixteen with no annotation to move. The escape-hatch clause is the sixth: replacing all twenty AI lines in `VmBoundedReader.cs` - every unit Security=High - with one sentence referring to nothing left both modes green. `Broiler.VM.Binary` is now closed to the hatch outright and every use elsewhere is counted and named in the component report. What that clause cannot do is judge a reason, which is EX-68. A FOURTH ROUND ATTACKED THE ENUMERATION RATHER THAN THE PREDICATE, and three of its four shapes are answered here, each with a witness: an enum member, which is how the budget dimensions and the reason codes are spelled, is now a unit and is exempt under case 8, because the enum DECLARATION is the unit that carries the vocabulary and its fingerprint covers every member and every value; a type declaration header is now a unit, because round one's permuted-ceiling defeat came back verbatim through a primary constructor, which has no body for case 2 to look at and was in no unit at all; and an event field declaration, the sibling of the field declarations the enumeration already had, is a unit and is deliberately not reached by case 7. A SECOND LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: the covered set is a directory enumeration and not the compiler evaluated `Compile` items, so a file the project pulls in from outside its own directory ships and is examined by nothing in this group. That is EX-63. A THIRD: the enumeration is a whitelist, and the fourth shape of that round - an `[assembly: InternalsVisibleTo]`, which is a member of nothing - can never be a unit however wide the list gets. Rule J7's file fingerprints are what answer that, not this rule.

rules.statement: Every assurance annotation in the product graph parses as two adjacent comment lines, or three where a falsification criterion stands between them, and every field on the AI line is in its closed vocabulary: `Origin`, `IP` and `Security` from their tables, `Resources` an integer 0 to 10, `Fingerprint` either `TBF` or six uppercase hex characters, `EXEMPT` a non-empty reason stated beside no other field, and nothing the system does not define. An assurance comment that does not parse, or that is attached to no declaration, is reported as stranded rather than ignored. A `Spec` value that cites an ADR names a record that exists under `docs/adr/`. A `// Broiler-Falsified-If:` line parses in that one place, states a criterion, states it on a single line, and carries no `Key=Value` field - it is prose, not data.
rules.evidence: Every annotation in the three product assemblies against `AssuranceAnnotation.VocabularyProblems` and `AssuranceScanner.OrphanAnnotations`
rules.nonVacuousWhen: 689 annotations are parsed and held to their vocabularies. Each closed vocabulary, each required field and each of the two malformed-exemption shapes carries a witness of its own: one witness with four bad fields would be satisfied by a check that reported the first, and three of the four vocabularies could then be deleted with the suite green. `Spec is optional` and is the only defined field that may be absent, so a rule requiring every defined field would reject the honest annotation on every unit that implements no frozen record. A block that does not parse is reported twice - once for the line that does not parse and once for the human line beneath it, which on its own opens no block - because half a block is the shape a hand-edited annotation leaves. The stranded clause has a witness whose only unit is exempt, so that the input violates this rule and not J1: a block describing a unit that is no longer there is how an annotation outlives its subject, and it is invisible to a coverage rule. The citation clause resolves the ADR NUMBER against the record set on disk and does no more: `Spec=ADR-9999 s42` is rejected because no record 9999 exists, and the section is not checked because the records carry no uniform section index. The falsification criterion carries four clauses with a witness each - an empty criterion, a criterion stating a field, a criterion wrapped onto a second line, and a criterion standing below the human line where the block parses without it - because they are four different ways the line stops being an instruction anybody can act on, and one witness carrying all four would be satisfied by a check that reported the first. The wrapped one is refused at the parse rather than trimmed, so the unit carries no annotation at all and J1 reports it too: a criterion that does not fit on a line is too vague to be one. THE LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: this rule checks that a value is IN its vocabulary and never that it is the RIGHT member of it. An annotation downgraded from `Security=High` to `Security=None` is well formed, and the generated header and the component report are derived from the annotations, so the downgrade is republished faithfully rather than reported as staleness. Nothing mechanical here can tell a correct assessment from a false one; the rubric that would decide it is prose in the component specification and the decision it asks for is a review. That is EX-65. The same limit applies to the criterion one field over, and harder: a criterion that parses, says something on one line and states no field satisfies this rule whatever it says. That is EX-75.

rules.statement: Every recorded AI fingerprint, as read from disk, equals the one the current declaration produces, and no human fingerprint names a version that is neither the current one nor preserved as `Previous`. The placeholder `TBF` is reported as its own fact, separately from a value that is simply wrong. A per-unit `EXEMPT=` annotation records no fingerprint and is not required to.
rules.evidence: Every annotated unit in the three product assemblies, scanned from the files as read from disk, against `AssuranceFingerprint.Of` over the declaration's token texts
rules.nonVacuousWhen: 689 annotated units each record a fingerprint the generator filled, and after a generation none records the placeholder - which is asserted, so the clean direction is not satisfied by a tree that has never been generated. The comparison reads the units AS THEY ARE ON DISK. Reading the generator output made this rule vacuous in its clean direction: every `Fingerprint` field there has already been rewritten to the recomputed value, so the rule compared a recomputed value against itself and editing a literal inside an annotated body left it green. Like J5 currency half it therefore runs in gate mode only, because a write run exists to refresh a fingerprint the code has outrun and asserting the pre-write value equalled the post-write value would fail every generation for a reason no reader could act on. The well-formedness assertion beside it reaches only units carrying a full assessment: an `EXEMPT=` line records no fingerprint, the specification documents that, J1 witnesses it being accepted, and applying the assertion to every annotated unit made the documented escape hatch unusable anywhere in the product tree. A `Previous=` fingerprint is accepted, because it is history and not a live approval; reporting it would punish the generator for recording what the policy requires it to record, and would push a reviewer towards deleting the history to get a green suite. The witness fingerprint is baked into the test rather than derived from the witness, because a witness that computed the value it is supposed to record would agree with itself whatever the fingerprinter did; the baked constant is asserted against the fingerprinter in the same test, so a change to normalization fails there and names it rather than quietly making four witnesses vacuous. THE FIRST LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: this rule reaches only ANNOTATED units, which is 689 of the 1,592 in the tree. The other 903 record no fingerprint in any source file and are covered by rule J7's manifest instead, which detects a change to them and reviews nothing. A SECOND LIMIT: six hex characters are 24 bits. The value answers whether this unit changed since it was reviewed and nothing else. It is not a collision-free identifier across units - a component with a few thousand units expects same-value pairs by the birthday bound - and it is not a cryptographic commitment: a party who can choose the code can find a preimage for a 24-bit prefix by brute force in seconds. Detecting a hostile rewrite that preserves the prefix is the job of the git history and the review event, not of this number. That is EX-61.

rules.statement: No unit is `VERIFIED` and no unit names a reviewer - live, or preserved as `Previous` - unless a human line in the source says so, and no generated artefact carries a human line reading anything but `PENDING`. The generator refuses, by exception, to rewrite a human line outside the four defined shapes at all, and to write any reviewer identifier the line it is reading does not already carry.
rules.evidence: Every annotated unit and every generated artefact against `AssuranceGenerator.RefuseInventedApproval` and the state machine
rules.nonVacuousWhen: 689 annotated units exist and every one of them reads `PENDING`, which is the honest state of this component and which the rule must not reject. Four generator transitions are witnessed separately - PENDING stays PENDING, an approval that left TBF is filled, a review the code has outrun becomes STALE with its reviewer and its approved version preserved, and a STALE line is not cleared by a recomputation - because the policy's forbidden edge is STALE straight to VERIFIED and one witness would pin only whichever branch fired first. The refusal is an exception rather than a report, so a bug that reached for a name fails loudly instead of quietly manufacturing an approval nobody gave, and it is driven THROUGH `DesiredSource` by a witness of its own rather than only by a direct call: the earlier witness called the guard directly, which pinned the function and not its wiring, so deleting its one call site left the suite green and the guard unreachable during a real generation. The shape clause is the other half of the same repair. A human body of `PENDING; Fingerprint=TBF` named nobody on either side of the name comparison, because the comparison skipped the reserved word wherever it appeared, while the annotation reader wanted exact equality and handed the head token back as a reviewer identifier - so a write run filled the fingerprint, resolved the unit to VERIFIED and published a human review of a line naming no human. Only the exact body `PENDING` now names nobody, and a body outside the four defined shapes is refused before anything is rewritten. The artefact half is asserted on the RENDERED text and not on the model, because a defect that produced the right unit state and the wrong line would be invisible to a check that read only the model - and it takes the artefact list as an argument so that it can be shown REJECTING one. Its only assertion used to be the accepting direction over the real tree, with no rejecting counterpart anywhere, so its whole body could be replaced by an empty list with nothing red. The witnesses carry the identifier WITNESS-ONLY, which appears nowhere outside that directory, because a rule about false approvals cannot be witnessed without an input containing one. THE FIRST LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: this rule refuses a name the tooling produced. It cannot refuse a name a human typed for someone else, or an invented one that reads plausibly - the same limit rule H4 records for the attestation. The policy answers it outside the source, in the pull-request history, and nothing in this component reads that history. A SECOND LIMIT: this rule reads HUMAN LINES, in the source and in the artefacts, and says nothing about the prose around them. A generated header that asserted a review in a sentence rather than on a human line was invisible to it, and rule J9 is what answers that.

rules.statement: Every generated file header, `CODE-ASSURANCE.md`, `HUMAN_REVIEW.md` and `assurance.manifest.json` is byte-identical to what the generator would produce from the annotations currently in the tree, and the component report's own figures - human reviewed, VERIFIED, unverified, the count of per-unit exemptions and the name of each one, the count of falsification criteria beside the count of units that owe one, and the plain statement that nothing has been reviewed - are true of the unit set it was generated from. Every generated file header states its own file's criteria count beside its security risk. No covered file carries more than one generated assurance block, and no covered file carries a line of the assurance summary vocabulary below the generated header, at any indentation and in any case.
rules.evidence: The 45 covered product source files, `CODE-ASSURANCE.md`, `HUMAN_REVIEW.md` and `assurance.manifest.json` against `AssuranceGenerator.Plan`, and the report's own rows against `AssuranceSummary.Of`
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Forty-eight artefacts are in the plan: one per covered product source file, plus the component report, the manifest and the human-review record - which is IN the plan rather than beside it, so the comparison that holds a file header to the tree holds the document a release is refused on. The currency comparison is one function, `AssuranceGenerator.StaleArtefacts`, asserted here and by the generator harness and witnessed by a deliberately stale artefact written to a real file and read back - the clause that gates the checkout previously had no witness at all, because every other J5 witness compares a string the test is holding against its own regeneration. The comparison is byte-identical, because 'equivalent' is what a stale summary always claims to be, and because the policy forbids a hand-maintained figure such as Human-reviewed: 47/47 outright. The currency half runs in gate mode only: under BROILER_ASSURANCE_WRITE=1 the same plan is being applied by the generator harness, and asserting that the pre-write text equals the post-write text would fail every generation for a reason no reader could act on. Every witness runs in both modes, so the rule is never a no-op. The report's figures are checked separately against the units they were computed from, because a byte comparison catches a report that has gone stale and cannot catch a generator that would compute a wrong figure and write it consistently - and the figure that matters most here is the one saying nothing has been reviewed. The per-unit exemption clauses are two, with a witness each - a report that states the count as zero while naming the unit, and a report that states the count and names nothing - because counting a use of the escape hatch and naming it are two different things a report can fail to do, and one witness would pin whichever fired first. One witness covers a hand-written SPDX pair with no generated marker under it, which is the shape every file in this component was in before its first generation and the shape that published the licence declaration twice. The forged-block clauses are stated separately from the byte comparison because a second summary block used to survive regeneration verbatim and become a fixed point, and because the byte difference it now produces does not say what is wrong: the fact a reader needs is that the file carries two summaries and one of them is a forgery. Both halves of that defence were defeated at once by INDENTING the forged block four spaces inside a class body, and a fourth round defeated what remained by WORDING one differently: the recogniser was a literal-string whitelist - exact ordinal equality against the banner and the marker, an ordinal StartsWith against its labels - so a block that shouts its labels, drops the banner and names a person was not a block at all. Both tests are now containment over an assurance summary vocabulary, case-insensitively, on comment lines anywhere below the generated header, and the vocabulary is checked against the product tree: none of its phrases appears in any comment below any generated header, so the clause costs nothing to adopt. The word `verified` is deliberately outside that vocabulary, because `VmVerifiedArtifact` is a public type of this component and its name appears in 112 lines below the generated headers; rule J9 is where that word is held, over the generated text alone. The criteria figures are asserted the same way the review figures are, against the units they were computed from rather than against the text: a header row and two report rows say how much of the high-risk surface carries a falsification criterion, and rule J10 is what names the units behind the shortfall. THE FIRST LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: the generator and the gate are the same code, and two lanes under `.github/workflows/` now compel it - the review lane regenerates every artefact on a pull request and commits what moved, and the publish lane runs the release mode before it packs. What a lane cannot do is what EX-60 is narrowed to: it runs on a pull request and on a tag, so a commit pushed to a branch nobody opens a pull request for is examined by nothing until the next one, and no lane compares a human line against its parent commit to decide whether a transition was legitimate. A SECOND LIMIT: no rule pins the INVOCATION of the currency comparison over the real tree. The function is witnessed and the two call sites both use it, so neither can drift from the other, and a patch deleting both call sites at once removes the gate with nothing red. That is EX-64. A THIRD, AND IT IS WHY RULE J8 EXISTS: this rule compares what is on disk against what the GENERATOR would write, so a sentence the generator itself invents is on both sides of the comparison and cannot be reported here at all.

rules.statement: No covered product source file contains any preprocessor directive - conditional or not - and the scanner parses every covered file with the conditional symbols the build defines.
rules.evidence: The 45 covered product source files against `AssuranceSources.DirectiveViolations` over the parse, and `AssuranceSources.ParseOptions`
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The product tree contains zero preprocessor directives, so the prohibition costs nothing to adopt and the clean direction is a fact about 45 files rather than a vacuous quantifier over none. The rule exists because a directive is TRIVIA, and trivia is what the fingerprint excludes so that a formatter cannot invalidate a review: parsed with no symbol defined, a `#if NET10_0_OR_GREATER` region the build COMPILES becomes disabled text, so a backdoor could be added to an annotated method with its recorded fingerprint unmoved, and a whole public method could ship outside the unit set entirely. That is the fingerprint's central claim - a semantically relevant change must invalidate - failing outright rather than a 24-bit collision. Two defences answer it and they are deliberately independent, each with its own clause and its own witness: the parse now defines a superset of what the SDK defines for net10.0 in both configurations, so a region that ships is scanned, annotated and fingerprinted like any other code and the witness asserts that no disabled text survives the parse; and this rule refuses the directive outright, with one witness for a conditional region - both its opening and its closing directive are named, because a rule reporting only the `#if` would accept a file whose region was opened where it could not see - and one for a `#pragma`, because the rule is about the whole class of directives and not about `#if`. THE LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: this rule reads the same corpus J1 does, so a compiled file outside the scanned set carries any directive it likes and is examined by nothing. That is EX-63. The symbol list is also a list: a target framework added later defines symbols this list does not, and the prohibition is what covers that gap rather than the list.

rules.statement: `assurance.manifest.json` covers EVERY code unit in the three product assemblies, exempt and relevant alike, each with its fully-qualified name, its file, its exemption state and the fingerprint of its declaration, AND every covered file whole, each with a fingerprint over the complete token stream of its compilation unit: every unit and every covered file present, no entry naming a unit or a file that is not there, and every recorded fingerprint and exemption state the one the current code produces. Nothing in a covered file can change without something moving here, whatever kind of declaration it is. The manifest is a change-detection record, not a review. An entry is not an assessment, not an approval and not evidence that anyone has read the unit; exempt units carry no annotation and no human line, and this rule moves none of them towards being reviewed.
rules.evidence: `assurance.manifest.json` as read from disk against `AssuranceManifest.Violations` over the units `AssuranceScanner` enumerates and the files `AssuranceSources` covers
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The manifest covers 1,592 units, of which 903 are exempt and therefore carry no annotation, no fingerprint in any source file and no review state - which is exactly the population this rule exists for - and 45 files, of which the ones declaring no code unit at all are covered by nothing else. Three adversarial rounds returned the same defeat in five different places and every one had one shape: the predicate answered EXEMPT, an exempt unit carries no annotation, an unannotated unit carries no fingerprint, and a unit with no fingerprint has no record of any kind. Narrowing the predicate case by case failed three times because each fix moved the defeat one case over. This rule separates the two questions that were fused: whether a unit needs a human annotation, which the predicate decides, and whether a unit is watched for change, which every unit is. A FOURTH ROUND THEN ATTACKED THE ENUMERATION ITSELF, which is the reason the file fingerprints exist. A unit entry is written only for a declaration kind the scanner names, and four shapes went through that whitelist with the suite green and this file byte-unchanged: an enum member, a type declaration header carrying a primary constructor, an event field declaration, and an `[assembly: InternalsVisibleTo]` that opens every internal type in `Broiler.VM.Runtime`. The first three are units now; the fourth is a member of nothing and can never be one, so a whitelist cannot be completed by adding to it. The six clauses are witnessed separately, because they are six different facts about a checkout and a witness asserted with a bare non-empty check would pin only whichever fired first: a unit present in the tree and missing from the manifest is a unit nothing watches; an entry for a unit that is not in the tree is a record of code that no longer exists; a recorded unit fingerprint that is not the current one is a unit that changed since the manifest was written; a covered file with no file entry is a file nothing watches WHOLE; a recorded file fingerprint that is not current is a file that changed outside every unit; and a file entry naming a file that is not covered is a record of a file that is gone. A seventh witness is the accepting direction over a manifest that covers its tree exactly, so the clean result is a comparison and not a function that reports nothing. An eighth is the assembly attribute itself, read under the tree's own name: the four units and their four fingerprints are asserted to be UNCHANGED by it, so the unit half of the record demonstrably reports nothing, and the file fingerprint is what moves. A ninth asserts that comments are outside the file token stream, which is not decoration: the generator writes a header into every covered file and two annotation lines above every relevant unit, and if either were in the stream the file's fingerprint would depend on the header, the header on the fingerprint, and no generation could ever be a fixed point. THE FIRST LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: detection is not review. A moved fingerprint is a line in a diff and a red suite until someone regenerates; nothing here assesses the change, no human line moves, and a developer may regenerate and accept any change to an exempt unit without anyone reading it. That is EX-67. A SECOND LIMIT: a moved FILE fingerprint says even less than a moved unit fingerprint - it does not say what moved, only that the file is not what it was, and locating the change is a diff a person reads. That is EX-69. A THIRD: the entries carry the same 24-bit fingerprint J3 records, with the same properties and the same non-properties, which is EX-61; and they cover the same directory-enumerated corpus J1 reads, so a compiled file outside that set is in no manifest, which is EX-63. Like J5's currency half, the comparison against the file on disk runs in gate mode only, because a write run exists to refresh it; the witnesses run in both modes.

rules.statement: Every generated artefact is line for line the artefact `AssuranceArtefactShape` declares: the manifest's `$comment` block, the sixteen-line generated header of every covered source file, the whole of `CODE-ASSURANCE.md` and the whole of `HUMAN_REVIEW.md`. Fixed text is held to a hand-maintained copy, so the generator cannot invent a sentence; derived content - every count, every portion, every distribution row, the worst assessed IP and Security risk, the list of high-security units, the per-file coverage table and the alias rows - is derived again here and compared by value.
rules.evidence: `AssuranceManifest.Header`, the generated header of each of the 45 covered source files, the generated `CODE-ASSURANCE.md` and the generated `HUMAN_REVIEW.md`, against `AssuranceArtefactShape`
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Forty-eight pieces of generated text are compared, and each is compared whole rather than by a handful of required phrases: 45 file headers of sixteen lines each, a 21-line manifest header, a component report of about two hundred lines and a human-review record of about three hundred. The record matters most of the four, because its subject is who has read what: a sentence invented in the generator would be a sentence about people, standing in the one place a reader goes to find out. The rule exists because rule J5 structurally cannot report what it reports. J5 compares what is on disk against what the GENERATOR would write, so a sentence the generator itself invents is on both sides of that comparison: two lines appended to `AssuranceManifest.Header` made the manifest assert reviewState=VERIFIED, humanReviewed=true, a named reviewer for every entry and that the component was eligible for release, with both modes of the gate green and every human line in the tree still reading PENDING. The mechanism is the one the group J register rows use - a second copy, kept by hand, compared for equality - and it is deliberately NOT generated from the generator, because a copy the generator produced would agree with the generator whatever the generator said. Where content is DERIVED it is derived again rather than copied, and by a different expression: the IP and Security rows walk their vocabulary from its weakest-claim end and stop at the first value some annotation carries, where `AssuranceSummary.Worst` ranks every annotation and takes a maximum, and the criteria row is counted from the LINE each block records where the generator asks its scanner. That is what pins `AssuranceSummary.Worst`, which feeds the two rows a developer actually reads at the top of every file and which nothing compared against the annotations they summarize. Four clauses have witnesses of their own: the two lines the attack appended to the manifest header, read from a witness and appended to the DECLARED header so the input is the forgery rather than a stale copy of the shape; a file header carrying a row the shape does not declare; a unit set whose three annotations are chosen so that a mistake in either direction changes the answer, with the accepting direction asserting that the generator and the shape agree on it and the rejecting direction asserting that a downgraded Security row is named with both texts; and the high-security list, asserted both by naming every High unit in the real report and by driving a report with one entry removed. The human-review record adds three more: a sentence put into the real record, the coverage table asserted to name every covered file, and the alias rows - which are the claim this document makes about PEOPLE, so the shape rebuilds them from the human lines where the generator asks `AssuranceHumanReview.Reviewers`, and the two are asserted to agree over a witness carrying two aliases, one whose decision the current code answers to and one the code has outrun. That witness is also the only place the multi-alias answer exists at all: nothing in this component names anybody, and the record must still have room for everybody. THE FIRST LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: a change made in BOTH places passes. A hand-maintained copy raises the cost of a forgery from one edit to two edits by someone who has read both; it does not make one impossible. That is EX-70, and rule J9 is the independent hold on the same text - it cannot be lifted by editing a shape. A SECOND LIMIT: the report witnesses are the REAL generated report with one line put into it rather than files on disk, because a stored copy of a generated artefact would be a second copy of the thing under test, would go stale at every regeneration, and would be repaired by regenerating it - which is the tautology this register exists to remove. The manifest-header and file-header witnesses are files, so the rule is not witnessed by mutation alone.

rules.statement: No generated text says verified, approved, reviewed by, a reviewer identifier or eligible for release unless the annotations support it. An occurrence is supported when the line states the count the annotations give for that term, or when a negation stands before the term on the same line. The corpus is the generated text alone: the whole of `CODE-ASSURANCE.md`, `HUMAN_REVIEW.md` and `assurance.manifest.json`, and the generated header block of a covered source file. A falsification criterion is a comment a human wrote below that header, and is not read here.
rules.evidence: The generated text of all 48 artefacts against `AssuranceReviewClaims.Violations` over the units the annotations produce
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The generated corpus DOES carry this vocabulary, in every artefact kind, and that is asserted rather than assumed: the report states `| VERIFIED | 0 |`, the manifest header states that an entry is not an approval, all 45 file headers state `Human-reviewed:`, and the human-review record states it in its headline - which is where the vocabulary matters most, because that record is the document a publish is refused on and the figure after the term is the only thing keeping the headline honest. Every one of those occurrences is supported, which is what makes the clean direction a comparison rather than a quantifier over nothing. The lie the generated record makes cheapest is witnessed by name: a `COMPLETE` headline over a tree in which nobody has recorded anything is reported with the count the annotations actually give. This is the policy's hardest rule - CI may never turn PENDING into a name - applied to the ARTEFACTS rather than to the source lines. Rule J4 holds every human line in every artefact to PENDING and says nothing about the prose around it, and prose is what a reader trusts: the two lines a fourth adversarial round appended to the manifest header were read by nothing in the suite. The count is DERIVED and not frozen at zero, which is witnessed: handed a unit set in which one unit is VERIFIED, the line `| VERIFIED | 0 |` becomes a violation and `| VERIFIED | 1 |` is accepted, so the rule follows the annotations rather than this milestone. It is deliberately independent of rule J8: J8's hand-maintained shape can be defeated by editing the shape as well as the generator, and this cannot be defeated by editing anything except the term list. The corpus is the generated text alone because `VmVerifiedArtifact` is a public type of this component and its name appears in 112 lines below the generated headers; a rule that read those would be reporting the component for having a domain, and the test asserts that those comments are outside what it reads. THE FIRST LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: the terms are a list, and a claim worded outside it is not seen - a generated sentence saying a unit was cleared, or signed, or passed, is not recognised. That is EX-71, and rule J8 is what covers it, because a sentence of any wording is a line the declared shape does not carry. A falsification criterion says what would make a unit wrong and asserts nothing about whether anybody looked, so it is outside this corpus by construction - it is a comment below the generated header - and that is witnessed in both directions: a criterion reading `a verified artifact is returned before the declared count is compared` is not reported, and the same line read as a whole-file corpus is. The one collision the third line actually produced was in the report's own prose about it: the sentence saying a criterion is an instruction to the REVIEWER states a term the annotations define no count for, so it was reworded rather than the rule weakened, and the original sentence is driven through the rule to show it would have been reported. A SECOND LIMIT: a negation standing before the term is accepted as a statement of absence, so a sentence that negates one thing and asserts another on the same line passes. Both limits are answered only by the two rules together, which is why neither is folded into the other.

rules.statement: Every unit assessed `Security=High` or `Security=Critical` carries a `// Broiler-Falsified-If:` line naming what would make it wrong, and every unit that owes one and carries none is reported by name. The line is permitted and not required below High. It is a comment, so it is outside every fingerprint by construction: rewording a criterion moves no unit fingerprint, no file fingerprint and no entry in `assurance.manifest.json`, and invalidates no review.
rules.evidence: Every annotated unit in the three product assemblies against `AssuranceScanner.MissingFalsificationCriteria`, and the three criteria on `src/Broiler.VM.Binary/VmBoundedAllocator.cs` against `AssuranceFingerprint.Of`, `AssuranceFingerprint.OfFile` and `AssuranceManifest.Render`
rules.nonVacuousWhen: THIS RULE IS RED AT THIS MILESTONE, WHICH IS THE CLAUSE WORKING. Forty-four units are assessed High or Critical; three of them - the whole of `src/Broiler.VM.Binary/VmBoundedAllocator.cs` - carry a criterion, and the rule names the other 41 one by one, because a count is a number a reader can do nothing with and a name is the declaration they have to write the criterion on. The clean direction is asserted last in the test, so that a reader who runs the suite sees the clause's own witnesses pass before they see the list of work it names. Both directions are witnessed: a High unit and a Critical unit carrying none are each named with the risk they were assessed at, and the Medium unit standing beside them is not, because below High the line is permitted and a rule that reported every unit without one would be a rule about comments rather than about the high-risk surface. `Security=High` is a set of forty-four units and not a test; the criterion is the test, and that is the whole reason the line exists. The fingerprint clause is asserted on the real file rather than on a probe: the three criteria are reworded, every unit fingerprint in the file is compared before and after, the file fingerprint over the complete token stream is compared, and the rendered manifest entries are compared - and the rewording is asserted to have happened, so a test that changed nothing would not pass it silently. That property is why a criterion may be edited freely: it is an instruction to the reviewer, not part of what they certify, so changing one must not invalidate an approval. THE FIRST LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: nothing here judges a criterion. A line reading `the code is wrong` parses, is one line, carries no field and satisfies this rule completely; whether the observation it names is the right one for that unit, and whether it is already unmet, is a review. That is EX-75, and it is the shape of EX-68's limit on the per-unit exemption reason one line down the block - a rule can hold a sentence to being present and cannot read it. A SECOND LIMIT: the requirement is driven by the annotation's own `Security` value, so a unit downgraded from High to Low owes no criterion and this rule reports nothing, which is EX-65 reached one field over. A THIRD: the line is a local extension to `BROILER-CODE-ASSURANCE.md`, which defines two lines and not three, and the owner may reject it. That is EX-74.

rules.statement: A tree may be published only when its assurance record says five things at once: every generated artefact on disk is what the generator would write; every annotation parses and states values this system defines, and no assurance comment is attached to nothing; every recorded fingerprint is the one its declaration produces now, and none is still the placeholder; every unit assessed `Security=High` or `Critical` carries a falsification criterion; and no relevant unit is left in a state that blocks a release. Each blocker is named with the declaration it is about, never counted. The gate is armed over this checkout by `BROILER_ASSURANCE_RELEASE=1`, which the publish lane sets and nothing else does.
rules.evidence: `AssuranceRelease.Blockers` over witness plans in both directions, and over `AssuranceGenerator.Current` when the publish lane arms it
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The five clauses are witnessed one at a time, because they are five different ways a green suite can sit over a tree nobody may publish and a witness asserted with a bare non-empty check would pin whichever fired first. The accepting direction is a tree in which every relevant unit carries a decision the current code answers to, which exists nowhere in this component and has to be synthesized: the gate would otherwise be a function nothing has ever seen succeed. THE REASON IT IS ARMED BY A VARIABLE, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: every relevant unit here is HUMAN_PENDING, and the owner has ruled that human review gates a release rather than a development step, so a gate that ran unconditionally would fail the suite over a tree that is exactly as the ruling permits. The FUNCTION is not conditional on anything - this rule drives it whatever the environment says - and only its application to this checkout is deferred to the lane that publishes. THE FIRST LIMIT: the fifth clause reads the states, and a state is only as good as the human line it was computed from. Rule J4 is what stops a line naming somebody nobody named, and neither rule can tell a real alias from an invented one, which is what EX-60 records that no lane closes. A SECOND LIMIT: this gate refuses a publish. It does not perform one, and nothing in this component asserts that the publish lane consults it - that binding is a workflow file, which is not under test here.
